pages.title: Burning Worlds
pages.text: There is a rite I record with shame. A dangerous Age may be quieted by feeding it the life of a calmer one. Only $(item)Descriptive Books$() hold enough of a world's soul for this. A linking book is only a road, and roads do not bleed enough.

Hold the $(c)Target Book$() in your main hand and the $(c)Sacrificial Book$() in your offhand. Crouch, then use the target. The rite answers only if the offered Age is steadier than the one you mean to save.

The rite compares the scores. Its reduction percentage is $(thing)(target - sacrifice) / 18$(), clamped between 1% and 60%. The target then loses that percentage of its current score, rounded upward. Thus a much steadier offering heals far more, but no single sacrifice removes over 60%.

The offered Age becomes a corpse and its family inherits the death: the root dimension data is erased, future terrain becomes void, heavens and weather are blanked, spawning and effects stop, and books become unreadable. Ordinary travelers are expelled; creative and spectator travelers may inspect the hollow.
